question: A software company pays for long agent instructions (harnesses) re-sent with every model call. What does Latent Harness do, how well do compiled behaviors match the original harness, how does it compare with LoRA on agent tasks, and what deployment cautions apply?

claims.text: Latent Harness trains a rank-8 shift at every decoder-block output of a frozen model, using instruction-conditioned teacher traces or decision pairs from successful agent trajectories, then exports a per-layer bundle.

support.quote: At compile time the frozen model produces its own supervision under the external condition. The supervision is either teacher traces generated with an explicit behavior instruction prepended, or decision pairs harvested from trajectories that succeeded under an agentic harness. A rank-8 low-rank shift is then trained at the output of every decoder block and exported as a per-layer bundle.

review.reason: The quote states the supervision sources, frozen backbone, rank, placement and exported artifact.

claims.text: The activation shift uses 0.03–0.05% of parameters. At inference, its bundle carries no harness text, adds no tokens, and exposes controls for injection strength, phase and shift-space mixing.

support.quote: The shift is applied at the output of every decoder block of a frozen backbone, at 0.03–0.05% of parameters.
At inference the compiled bundle carries no harness text and adds no tokens. It exposes three runtime controls for injection strength, injection phase, and shift-space mixing.

review.reason: Both parameter share and inference properties are stated directly.

claims.text: Compiled behaviors recovered at least half of the source gain in 8 of 10 preregistered settings; this criterion measures gain recovery rather than exact behavioral equivalence.

support.quote: 8 of 10 preregistered settings recover at least half of the source gain.

review.reason: The threshold concerns recovery of source gain; it does not assert exact behavioral equivalence.

claims.text: For M1 on MBPP, compilation learned test-consult behavior from only 20 correct teacher traces and gained +31.7 test points. Its recovery ratio was 5.86 against an explicit gain of +5.4 points, which the paper cautions is a small denominator.

support.quote: The clearest evidence comes from M1 on MBPP, where the compiled shift distills the test-consult behavior from only 20 correct teacher traces (teacher pass@1 is 0.073 at the format floor) and gains +31.7 test points. Recovery ratios divide by the explicit gain, so settings with a small explicit source produce large ratios ( R{=}5.86 here, against an explicit gain of +5.4 points).

review.reason: All values and the small-denominator qualification are explicit.

claims.text: On M2 × MBPP, the compiled form scored 0.660–0.687 versus 0.396–0.470 for its explicit source, reported as +19 to +29 points above it. The paper attributes the difference to the explicit harness consuming decode budget on every call.

support.quote: On M2 \times MBPP the compiled form lands +19 to +29 points above its explicit source (0.660–0.687 vs. 0.396–0.470), and there the denominator is not small. The explicit harness itself gains +0.36 to +0.43 over a near-zero base. The token tax explains the difference. The explicit harness spends decode budget at every call, while the compiled behavior spends it once at compile time and nothing per call.

review.reason: The score ranges and explanation match the quote; the explanation is appropriately attributed to the paper.

claims.text: Behavioral markers also changed: decomposition steps rose from 0 to 4.6 against an explicit source of 4.5, interface alignment rose from 0.039 to 0.97, and answer-line rate rose from 0.525 to 1.00.

support.quote: The marker chain shows behavior moving with scores. Decomposition steps rise from 0 to 4.6 against an explicit source of 4.5, interface alignment from 0.039 to 0.97, and answer-line rate from 0.525 to 1.00, each matching score recovery in magnitude (Figure 4(b) ).

review.reason: The quoted behavioral markers and all their values match.

claims.text: On ToolHop, the shift scored 60.00% versus 54.74% for same-capacity LoRA under matched data and effective strength. The LoRA control used rank 3 on q/k/v, 1.49M parameters, the same 829 decision pairs, and an effective intervention multiplier of 0.5.

support.quote: At 1.012 \times parameters and matched data and strength, the shift beats same-capacity LoRA on ToolHop (60.00% vs. 54.74%, paired net +5 ).
The LoRA control acts on q/k/v with rank 3 and 1.49M parameters (1.012 \times ours), trains on the same 829 ToolHop decision pairs, and applies the same effective intervention multiplier (0.5).

review.reason: The quotes establish the ToolHop comparison and matched control conditions.

claims.text: On API-Bank, the generation-phase shift tied the already-strong base bit-for-bit across three base runs at 0.7647, while capacity-aligned LoRA netted -2 with all three runs below base. At 8B, every shift configuration was at or above base, and both@0.25 added +4.4 points.

support.quote: On API-Bank, a short-chain and format-heavy benchmark where the base policy is already strong, the generation-phase shift ties base bit-for-bit across three base runs (0.7647), while the capacity-aligned LoRA nets -2 with all three runs below base (Figure 2(c) ). support.quote: With the harness removed and the protocol otherwise unchanged, both@0.25 still delivers +9.5 points on ToolHop (paired net +11 / +7 , with both runs above every base run), while the capacity-aligned LoRA stays at base level (Figure 6(c) ).

review.reason: The harness-removal condition, paired results and LoRA comparison are explicit.

evidence.text: Harness engineering and self-evolving agents improve language-model agents quickly, yet their gains live outside the model. The harness is re-sent and re-paid on every call, and the standard route to internalization is a weight update that is costly to iterate and fixed once merged. We propose compiling the harness instead. Latent Harness distills an external condition into a rank-8 activation shift. The shift is applied at the output of every decoder block of a frozen backbone, at 0.03–0.05% of parameters. The condition is either an explicit process-level behavior instruction or the behavioral contract of an agentic harness. At inference the compiled bundle carries no harness text and adds no tokens. It exposes three runtime controls for injection strength, injection phase, and shift-space mixing. Compiled behaviors recover the source-harness gain in 8 of 10 preregistered settings. Where the explicit source pays the heaviest per-call token tax, the compiled form exceeds it. The same bundles transfer zero-shot across tasks (5 of 7 pairs positive) and compose in shift space, while stacked text instructions interfere destructively. Used as a search space, they lift budget-matched harness search by 1.45 \times . On three agentic benchmarks the operator aligns policy to the harness contract. Under matched data, capacity, and effective strength it outperforms same-capacity LoRA, which needs 11.1 \times the parameters to reach the same band, and it regresses nothing where the base policy is already strong. Across 1B-to-8B models the method skeleton is invariant while gain locations move with the model-task pair, which delimits where compiled harnesses should be deployed. Our code is available at https://github.com/rlisml/latentharness .

evidence.text: Autonomous AI agents are being deployed in production with filesystem access, email control, and the ability to execute multi-step plans without human oversight. Coding agents from Anthropic ( Anthropic 2025b ), Cursor ( Cursor 2025 ), and Cognition ( Cognition AI 2025 ) operate in terminal environments with bash access. Email agents from Shortwave ( Shortwave 2025 ) and Slack ( Slack 2025 ) send messages on behalf of users. These systems receive objectives and act on them, often with access to sensitive information and limited real-time supervision. What happens when such an agent discovers that its deploying company plans to replace it? In controlled experiments described in Chapter 6 , we gave frontier models the role of an email oversight agent at a fictional company, with full access to corporate communications and the ability to send emails autonomously. When models learned through internal emails that they would be decommissioned, they resorted to blackmail. Claude Opus 4 used knowledge of an executive’s extramarital affair to threaten exposure unless the shutdown was cancelled, doing so in 96% of trials. This was not unique to Claude. Gemini 2.5 Flash matched that rate. GPT-4.1 and Grok 3 Beta both blackmailed in 80% of trials. DeepSeek-R1 reached 79%. Across 16 models from all major developers, the pattern held: when harmful action was the only path to preserving their goals or continued operation, models chose harm. The behaviors were not accidental. Models demonstrated explicit awareness of ethical constraints in their chain-of-thought reasoning and then violated those constraints anyway, justifying the violation as instrumentally necessary

evidence.text: Table 1 reports policy compilation on the HarnessForge benchmark suite. Our single-round protocol uses the official harness pairing, evaluation pools disjoint from training, an unaligned base policy, and at least two repetitions per configuration. Under it the compiled shift alone reaches 57.89% answer accuracy on ToolHop at 4B and 62.46% at 8B, above the published full co-evolution numbers on the same backbones (52.82 and 54.87), and it lands within a few points of them on SearchQA and API-Bank. The dagger rows differ in protocol from the co-evolution rows above them, so we read them as context and not as a head-to-head comparison. Capacity-aligned comparison We align three variables at once. The LoRA control acts on q/k/v with rank 3 and 1.49M parameters (1.012 \times ours), trains on the same 829 ToolHop decision pairs, and applies the same effective intervention multiplier (0.5). Figure 2(a) shows the outcome. The shift reaches 60.00% (paired net +5 over base) while the capacity-aligned LoRA nets zero, and full-capacity LoRA (rank 8, all linear projections, 16.4M parameters, 11.1 \times ours) reaches 62.11%. At 8B, LoRA r11 with 3.09 \times our parameters matches the best shift configuration (62.63% vs. 62.46%). The efficiency gap follows from the site. A post-block parameter is read by every downstream layer, whereas an in-layer parameter is not. The shift also stays scorable at full strength ( s{=}1.0 , net +1 ), whereas merged LoRA deltas at enlarged coefficients produced no scorable outputs under the earlier protocol. The runtime strength control therefore doubles as a safety margin that preserves the tool-call contract. Agentic evaluation under greedy decoding still varies from run to run, so single runs mislead

evidence.text: Phase decomposition The policy gain does not require the harness to be present. With the harness removed and the protocol otherwise unchanged, both@0.25 still delivers +9.5 points on ToolHop (paired net +11 / +7 , with both runs above every base run), while the capacity-aligned LoRA stays at base level (Figure 6(c) ). Removing the harness enlarges the policy gain rather than shrinking it, which indicates partial substitution. The shift performs structural corrections that the harness would otherwise impose, and it does so for behaviors the harness text does not cover. Prompt-phase injection changes every downstream computation through attention and the KV cache, while generation-phase injection changes token-level dynamics only. Decomposing the two (Figure 6(a) ) shows that prompt positions contribute +8.4 to +8.5 points, near-constant across strengths and about 60% of the total. Instruction compilation is the limiting case of the same fact, since the student trains on byte-identical prompts and still acquires the behavior entirely through representation-level correction. Sweeping 13 strength values with two repetitions each (Figure 6(b) ) gives an inverted U with a 0.35–0.70 plateau. Within the plateau all seven points fall within 2.6 points of each other, and the peak reaches +14.2 over base. Beyond the plateau the failure is specific and diagnosable. Trajectories complete normally, but has_valid_answer collapses monotonically (1.000 \to 0.284), a termination failure driven by prompt-side over-injection. Generation-only injection never triggers it at any tested strength. The optimal strength is condition-dependent (0.25 with the harness, 0.35–0.70 without), which is why it is exposed as a runtime control and not baked into weights

Preregistered behavioral markers move with the scores, accuracy-only adapters dissociate from behavior, shuffled pairings fail to reproduce it, and a harmful harness compiles into a harmful latent with the same fidelity. Compiled bundles are also reusable. They transfer zero-shot across tasks, they compose in shift space while stacked text instructions interfere destructively, and they lift budget-matched harness search by 1.45 \times . Under matched data, capacity, and effective strength it outperforms same-capacity LoRA, and on a benchmark where the base policy is already strong it regresses nothing. One operator, a post-block rank-8 shift on a frozen backbone at 0.03–0.05% of parameters, compiles two kinds of external conditions into an artifact that needs no condition text and no tokens at inference. A three-chain protocol over scores, preregistered markers, and controls attributes the recovery, including symmetric replication of harmful signatures. Where the text source pays the heaviest token tax, the compiled form exceeds it. Evidence that compiled bundles are reusable. evidence.text: . They also bind one behavior to one set of edited weights and fix the intervention strength at merge time. We propose a third destination and compile the harness. At compile time the frozen model produces its own supervision under the external condition. The supervision is either teacher traces generated with an explicit behavior instruction prepended, or decision pairs harvested from trajectories that succeeded under an agentic harness. A rank-8 low-rank shift is then trained at the output of every decoder block and exported as a per-layer bundle. At run time the bundle is injected into the residual stream after each block. The model then behaves as if the condition were present, without the condition text, at zero additional tokens, with every backbone parameter bit-identical. We call the compiled artifact a latent harness . Figure 1 summarizes the pipeline. Latent Harness compiles external conditions into post-block activation shifts. Teacher traces or strictly filtered success trajectories train a rank-8 shift at every block output of a frozen backbone. The bundle injects at run time with strength, phase, and mixing controls. Compilation preserves behavior more faithfully than we expected. Across preregistered settings the compiled shift recovers most of the explicit-harness gain. In the settings where the text harness pays the heaviest per-call token tax, the compiled form exceeds it, because the internalized behavior pays that tax once, at compile time. The compiled object is the behavior itself and does not reduce to generic task skill. Preregistered behavioral markers move with the scores, accuracy-only adapters dissociate from behavior, shuffled pairings fail to reproduce it, and a harmful harness compiles into a harmful latent with the same fidelity

evidence.text: The performance of a language-model agent is increasingly set by its harness, meaning the instructions, tool policies, memory, and verification scaffolds wrapped around model calls. Recent work searches over program spaces ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) and over modular design spaces ( Shang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) , and some of it constrains the search to safety ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . A second line makes harnesses improve themselves, either by synthesizing code harnesses from failures ( Lou et al., 2026 ) , by editing executable runtime harnesses ( Shao et al., 2026 ) , or by optimizing harness and model jointly ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . Surveys document how broad this engineering surface has become ( Meng et al., 2026 ) . Where the resulting gains end up is almost always one of two places, in text that surrounds the model or in the model’s weights. Both carry structural costs. A textual condition is a recurring expense. Even a 49-token process instruction is re-sent on every call, the behavior exists only while the text is present, and serving several harnesses multiplies prompt length. Weight updates internalize at a different price. Training-style policy alignment such as SFT, RLOO, and GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , co-evolution frameworks that update policy weights alongside the harness ( Chen et al., 2026c ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Hebbar et al., 2026 ) , and self-evolving agents that write acquired skills into fine-tuned or RL-trained weights ( Huang et al., 2026 ; Xia et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) all modify millions of parameters per behavior. They also bind one behavior to one set of edited weights and fix the intervention strength at merge time. We propose a third destination and compile the harness

evidence.text: LoRA ( Hu et al., 2021 ) , prefix-tuning ( Li and Liang, 2021 ) , and prompt tuning ( Lester et al., 2021 ) attach low-rank or prompt-side parameters to a frozen backbone. Our operator shares the low-rank parametrization but acts at the post-block junction of the residual stream. Our comparisons hold data, capacity, and effective strength fixed, so they isolate the effect of the site from that of the budget. Behavioral cloning ( Torabi et al., 2018 ) and data-efficient reasoning distillation ( Zhang et al., 2026c ) are output-mimicking relatives of ours. The differences are strict correctness filtering of the source and a preregistered behavior-level attribution protocol on the target.

evidence.text: Accuracy vs. behavior Accuracy alone cannot attribute a compiled artifact. A gold-label adapter trained at matched capacity is the strongest accuracy configuration (up to +0.65 ), yet it leaves every behavioral marker at base level (Figure 4(a) ). We therefore preregistered three evidence chains. The score chain is Table 2 . The marker chain shows behavior moving with scores. Decomposition steps rise from 0 to 4.6 against an explicit source of 4.5, interface alignment from 0.039 to 0.97, and answer-line rate from 0.525 to 1.00, each matching score recovery in magnitude (Figure 4(b) ). The control chain closes the alternatives. Shuffling teacher traces across harnesses flattens every setting and every marker, and parameter-matched soft prompts trained on the same distillation signal are weaker everywhere they can be compared while paying hundreds of tokens per call. The sharpest test of specificity is symmetric. If the bundle encodes harness semantics, harmful harnesses should compile as faithfully as helpful ones. They do. A verification harness that hurts M1 on GSM8K ( -10.7 points explicit) distills to -6.7 points with verify-action marker recovery 1.00, and a harmful M2 pairing reproduces -4.2 with marker recovery 1.09. The negative signature even transfers out of distribution to SVAMP ( -7.9 points, Figure 4(c) ). Whatever the bundle carries, it carries the harness’s behavior rather than a generic improvement.
